title: Slot-based batch credits + per-vector delta pricing for embeddings & rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Enterprise customers ask for clearer per-vector economics while wanting predictable unit cost for high-volume rerank/embedding workloads. Current per-vector billing is simple but penalizes bursts and discourages bulk offload workflows (indexing, nightly reranks). Goal: introduce a hybrid pricing primitive that preserves per-vector transparency while offering slot-based batch credits for heavy throughput -- reducing sticker price for sustained bulk workflows without creating accounting complexity in contracts or breaking existing committed customers.

Proposal summary: 
- Introduce "slot credits": customers purchase monthly slots (small integer tiers) which convert to pre-paid vector consumption credits for embeddings and rerank endpoints. Slots have volume buckets and a time-bound validity (monthly).
- Keep a visible per-vector base price; slots apply a discounted effective per-vector rate for vectors consumed from slot credit pools.
- Offer a per-vector delta for rerank flows (reranks count as N vectors based on candidates * queries) with configurable caps to avoid misuse.
- Billing/usage model: slot purchases reduce per-vector usage from the regular metered bucket; overage falls back to per-vector list price. Slot sizes: pilot tiers: 500K, 2M, 10M vectors/month.

Experiment design: 
- Pilot cohort (3 enterprise customers) on dedicated Dedicated/Dedicated-sim accounts to validate integration and accounting downstream.
- Self-serve beta for existing high-volume customers (opt-in) exposed through the Console with cost estimates and a charge-sim tool.
- A/B test: compare conversion rate, average effective $/vector, margin, and churn across pilot vs control over 8 weeks. Key metrics: effective $/vector, committed ARR uplift, net revenue retention, billing disputes, and support tickets.

Engineering scope & risks: 
- Billing: add slot SKU, credit consumption logic in billing pipeline, reconciliation jobs, and invoice labels (ENG-83421).
- Runtime: no changes to inference runtime; ensure usage tagging supports slot attribution (request header or billing token).
- Console: new purchase flow, quota dashboard, and cost simulator.
- SDK/API: optional header for slot attribution; backward compatible.
- Risks: inaccurate usage attribution on retries, double-dipping on cached KV hits, and possible revenue cannibalization if slot discounts are too aggressive. Mitigations: conservative discounting, attribution tests, and quota enforcement.

Enterprise QSA / Contract items: 
- Update QSA talking points for pricing changes: how billing events are generated, retention windows for usage logs (90 days by default), and dispute resolution timelines.
- Add contract language templates for slot commitments, overage mechanics, and audit access.
- Legal request: classify slot purchases as billable one-month commitments with pro-rated termination behavior; confirm with Legal/Finance on revenue recognition.

Rollout plan: 
1) Internal pilot (April): billing + console + 3 pilot customers.
2) Beta (May): self-serve opt-in + SDK docs + pricing page.
3) GA (June): full catalog, partner QSA readout, and marketplace listing.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Exact slot sizing and discount % (suggest starting with 10-25% effective discount vs list depending on tier).
- How to surface slot usage for multi-team orgs (per-route attribution vs account-wide).
- Whether to allow cross-product slots (embeddings + rerank) or keep separate pools.

Acceptance criteria for pilot: 
- Billing accuracy within 0.5% in reconciliation runs for 30 days.
- No customer-visible latency or error increases.
- Pilot customers sign MOU for the slot pilot and confirm QSA clarifications.

Artifacts: PRD and simulation workbook (see links).
